headline: University of Kentucky staffer wins religious exemption from mandatory AI use
summary: A University of Kentucky research administrator was granted a Title VII religious exemption allowing him to avoid using AI tools at work, Tom's Hardware and TechCrunch both report. TechCrunch names him as David Durman; Tom's Hardware describes the case, per the American Humanist Association, as the first of its kind.

claims.statement: A University of Kentucky research administrator was granted a Title VII religious exemption from mandatory AI use at work.

sources.quote: A research administrator at the University of Kentucky was granted a Title VII exemption, allowing them to not use AI tools as it goes against their moral beliefs.
David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, recently earned a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.
